results.summary: This project is a low-footprint scan chain for the iHP PDK / SG13CMOS5L, written in Verilog. It uses a single chain with one bit per byte, built from RS flip-flops made from sg13g2_a21o_1 cells, and includes an internal free-running counter. Control pins SC_RESET, SC_CLK, SC_GET, SC_SET, SC_DIN, and SC_DOUT manage the chain, while DO0-DO8 and DI0-DI7 provide parallel data access. It is intended to be driven by a microcontroller or CPU, likely a Raspberry Pi.

results.summary: This project is a 1-bit vector-matrix multiplier coprocessor for accelerating Binary Neural Networks on a 1x1 tile. It contains eight physical neurons, each with an 8-bit weight shift register and a 10-bit accumulator, using XNOR multiplication and a popcount adder tree. There is no internal state machine; a host processor handles looping, routing, and layer management. The chip is driven by a host microcontroller that loads weights, streams binarized pixels, pulses compute, and reads the accumulator output.

results.summary: Elemental Harmony is a silicon-native 4x4 strategy game implemented as a TinyTapeout module in Verilog. It uses a 16-bit occupancy register and a finite state machine to coordinate turns between a human player and an internal logic engine. The engine uses an LFSR to find empty tiles and scores adjacent elemental pattern matches with a combinational adder tree. Error states stream the board occupancy and fill count back to the interface so a move can be retried without a full reset.
